nodes.summary: A list `π` of clauses is a resolution derivation from `φ` when every line is a clause of `φ` or follows from earlier lines by the resolution rule or the weakening rule (Ben-Sasson and Wigderson, J. ACM 48 (2001), Section 2.1). Its size is the length of `π`.
nodes.title: Resolution derivation

nodes.summary: A resolution derivation from `φ` whose last line is the empty clause.
nodes.title: Resolution refutation

nodes.summary: The clause $C$ may follow the lines `earlier` in a resolution derivation from $\varphi$ when it is a clause of $\varphi$, the resolvent on some variable $x$ of two earlier lines (one containing $x$, the other $\neg x$), or a weakening of an earlier line (it contains all of that line's literals).
nodes.title: One step of a resolution derivation

nodes.summary: The largest width of one of its clauses, `0` for the empty formula (Ben-Sasson and Wigderson, J. ACM 48 (2001), Section 2.3).
nodes.title: Width of a CNF formula

nodes.summary: A formula with a resolution refutation is unsatisfiable.
nodes.title: A refutation proves unsatisfiability

nodes.summary: A formula with a tree-like derivation of the empty clause is unsatisfiable.
nodes.title: A tree-like refutation proves unsatisfiability

nodes.summary: The number of lines (nodes) of the tree.
nodes.title: Size of a tree-like derivation

nodes.summary: The largest width of a line of the tree.

nodes.title: Ben-Sasson–Wigderson for general resolution

nodes.summary: A tree-like derivation of the clause `C` from the clauses of `φ`: a leaf is a clause of `φ`, an inner node applies the resolution rule (from `E ∨ x` and `F ∨ ¬x` derive `E ∨ F`) or the weakening rule (from `E` derive any clause containing all literals of `E`). Clauses of `φ` may be used at several leaves (Ben-Sasson and Wigderson, J. ACM 48 (2001), Section 2.1).
nodes.title: Tree-like resolution derivation

nodes.summary: Every line of a resolution derivation from `φ` holds under every assignment satisfying `φ`.
nodes.title: Soundness of resolution derivations

nodes.summary: Every clause with a tree-like derivation from `φ` holds under every assignment satisfying `φ`.
nodes.title: Soundness of tree-like resolution

nodes.summary: If a CNF formula $F$ has a tree-like refutation with $S$ lines, then it has a resolution refutation of width at most $w(F) + \log_2 S$, where $w(F)$ is the largest width of a clause of $F$. It is stated as $2^{\text{width}} \le 2^{w(F)} \cdot S$. Equivalently, the minimal tree-like refutation size satisfies
nodes.title: Ben-Sasson–Wigderson for tree-like resolution

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
